input: Audience: Owners of all-inclusive wedding venues whose prospective couples compare their package with local venue-only options and ask what the total wedding will involve or cost. | Tension: Couples may see a venue-only rental figure beside a larger all-inclusive price without yet knowing the services, items, and planning responsibilities represented by either option. | Argument: When couples compare an all-inclusive venue with venue-only alternatives, showing what each option includes and what couples would need to source separately can make the comparison more meaningful than headline rental fees alone. | Take: Help couples compare the scope and responsibilities of the options before treating the visible venue fee as a like-for-like price comparison. | Mechanism: The venue owner said couples ask what is included and what the wedding will cost. She described using a comparison chart and estimated outside costs in tour follow-up; making comparable scope visible can help buyers evaluate what they would otherwise need to arrange, while the account does not establish a tested effect on bookings. | Reader decision: Inspect the comparison material and follow-up: does it clearly show what the package includes and distinguish that from estimated costs and tasks couples may take on elsewhere?
